an10.40:1.1: “Bhante, it is said: ‘Concord in the Saṅgha, concord in the Saṅgha.’
an10.40:1.2: How is there concord in the Saṅgha?”
an10.40:1.3: “Here, Ānanda, (1) bhikkhus explain non-Dhamma as non-Dhamma … as in 10:38 … and (10) what has been prescribed by the Tathāgata as having been prescribed by him.
an10.40:1.4: On these ten grounds they do not withdraw and go apart. They do not perform legal acts separately or recite the Pātimokkha separately. It is in this way,
an10.40:1.5: Ānanda, that there is concord in the Saṅgha.”
an10.40:2.1: “But, Bhante, when one reconciles a divided Saṅgha, what does one generate?”
an10.40:2.4: “One rejoices in heaven for an eon, Ānanda.”
an10.40:3.1: Pleasant is concord in the Saṅgha,
an10.40:3.2: and the mutual help of those who live in concord. Delighting in concord,
an10.40:3.4: one does not fall away from security from bondage.
an10.40:3.5: Having brought concord to the Saṅgha,
an10.40:3.6: one rejoices in heaven for an eon.
